v.rationale: All three pass their suites, and all handle the core requirements: dispatch after commit, an account-wide 5 requests/second limit, skipping cancelled orders, failing a 422 without retry, recording the reason when retries run out, an idempotency key, and a database claim so the email goes out once. Probes ran through a real database queue and worker. impl-1 ranks first. Its markAsPaid uses an atomic conditional UPDATE, which prevents double dispatch and refuses to pay soft-deleted orders. It handles 429 most robustly: it honours Retry-After, clamps the delay to 1..120s, and falls back to 30s when the header is missing or a date. Its tests make the best use of withFakeQueueInteractions. Its weak points are a manual failed() call in the 422 test and a generic 'attempted too many times' reason when 429s persist. impl-2 is the leanest and was correct in every probe. It loses ground for an unlocked paid check, no paid-status guard in the job, and ignoring Retry-After. impl-3 has a real throttling bug: an HTTP-date Retry-After produces release(0), so the job immediately hits the throttled partner again. It also treats every other 4xx as a permanent failure, which goes beyond the spec and is risky. It has more branching ceremony and a less idiomatic HTML mail view, so it ranks last.
